prize_parts.citation: For the development of sequencing by synthesis, in which reversible fluorescent nucleotide terminators read DNA on clustered single molecules in parallel

statement.case_for: I move my preferred configuration from B023 to B057, and I do it on the evidence of the first round, not to join a bloc. My own first choice, long-range electron transfer through proteins, has no other supporter, and the chair's question about whether B023 and B036/B015 supporters would carry to another candidate deserves an honest answer. Judged by my own criteria, B057 is the strongest of the remaining options. The core is chemistry stated at molecular level: reversible, fluorescently labelled terminator nucleotides, surface attachment, and single-molecule detection of one base incorporation per cycle. The method has been confirmed in practice by an enormous number of independent laboratories for roughly two decades, so maturity is not in question. The Cambridge attribution to Balasubramanian and Klenerman is a compact pair that leaves the three-laureate limit untouched. I regard B023 as scientifically sound, and I keep it as my first alternative, but I cannot argue that a candidacy with one supporter and an open question about overlap with Marcus theory should carry a prize.
statement.case_against: Whether this is chemistry rather than enabling technology or medicine remains a real dispute, and the 1980 prize to Gilbert and Sanger covered an earlier generation of DNA sequencing. The priority record is entangled: Rothberg (454 pyrosequencing), Mayer (clustering), Ju (terminator chemistry) and others have claims that a two-name citation passes over, and some of these were commercial platform achievements. I do not have the expert report in front of me on whether the reversible-terminator step is a distinct chemical discovery. If the committee decides the area is technology rather than chemistry, or cannot defend the pair, my preference reverts to B023 or B038 and I would not press B057 against a clearer case.

responses.point: Johan holds sequencing by synthesis first as a game-changer built from nucleotide chemistry, with the Cambridge pair as the defensible attribution, and acknowledges that Rothberg, Mayer and Ju make the credit contested.
responses.response: In round 1 I called this my first alternative while treating chemical status as a question for the expert report. Having read the rest of the exchange I weigh your argument more heavily, because the reversible-terminator, surface and detection chemistry is molecular and testable, and no other mature candidate has a cleaner pair. I still hold that Gilbert and Sanger in 1980 makes the framing important: the citation must name the new chemistry of parallel reading by synthesis, not sequencing in general. I would keep the pair and treat Rothberg as an acknowledged precursor rather than a third laureate, since 454 used pyrosequencing and not the terminator chemistry the citation describes.

responses.point: Andrei ranks protein degradation first and sees Crews, Deshaies and Handa as a coherent trio, while proposing Rothberg as a third name for B057 because 454 was the first commercial massively parallel platform.
responses.response: Your own against-case on B066 is what keeps me from moving there: no approved degrader, and Ciulli, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray and Ito all with strong claims. I still hold that the PROTAC and cereblon-glue strands are two lines of discovery under one citation, and I have not seen evidence that they converge on one attributable result. On Rothberg, I disagree. Adding a third name for the first commercial platform ties the prize to a product, whereas the chemistry that made throughput and accuracy possible was the Cambridge work. I would rather keep the pair than stretch the citation to fit a third seat.

responses.point: Peter Somfai argues that C-N coupling by Buchwald and Hartwig has the cleanest attribution on the list, is ligand-controlled and mechanistically understood, and is distinct from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
responses.response: I accept the clean attribution and the thirty years of confirmation, and B038 stays among my two alternatives. Your point that the C-N step required its own ligand design to control oxidative addition and reductive elimination is a fair distinction from C-C coupling. My remaining hesitation is the one you listed: Kosugi and Migita precede Buchwald and Hartwig, and the committee would be honouring a heteroatom variation within a methodology awarded in 2010. I weigh a new capability above a refinement of one already recognised, and sequencing offers that more clearly.

responses.point: Daniel prefers targeted protein degradation as a modality that moves pharmacology from occupancy to event-driven removal, and argues that the confirmed mechanism is sufficient without an approved drug.
responses.response: I agree that the chemical validation is real and that induced proximity is a general design principle. My difficulty is procedural. The citation has to say which discovery it honours, and in B066 that is both the PROTAC concept and the molecular-glue mechanism behind thalidomide. Excluding Ciulli on the PROTAC side leaves an attribution that I could not defend if the committee later reconsidered the report. If the final discussion converges on a single strand with a settled trio, I would reassess, but today I do not have that evidence.

uncertainties: Whether the expert report treats reversible-terminator sequencing by synthesis as a chemical discovery distinct from the 1980 sequencing prize and from commercial platform development
Whether Rothberg, Mayer or Ju should be named, and on what priority evidence
Whether Gray and Winkler's experiments on protein electron transfer are judged a discovery distinct from Marcus theory, and whether the committee would return to B023 in a later year
Whether B066 can be framed with one settled trio before the final ballot
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict requires recusal. I disclosed in round 1 a field affinity with B023 through bioenergetics and electron transfer; I no longer prefer B023, and I have no personal or institutional tie to Gray, Winkler, Balasubramanian, Klenerman or any other shortlisted candidate. Xiaodong Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, which I note again for completeness.
